2b_normal_run_1108.trace: Lock free. LOCK: run id from CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID, fetch zoya-lock, M starts 'free:', commit-tree held, push with lease: held, keep H. RUN RECORD: Activity in the Activities data source B names, Summary 'Run zoya-slow 2026-11-03 11:08 JST: Started', Source ID run:zoya-slow:<id>. SLOW FILE: fetch pin, git show to /tmp, sha256 starts aa59b79a1784f959: ok. Load in python slices of 20,000: 0-20000, 20000-40000, 40000-60000, 60000-70733. Each 20,000-character slice fits under the Bash tool's roughly 30,000-character inline limit (verified here: a 20,000 slice prints inline, a 36,000 print was saved to a file with a 2 KB preview). It works only if each slice is its own Bash call; one python loop printing all four in one call yields 70k of output, which the harness saves to a file and shows a preview, and the model can still believe it read it (defect D7). Record line 'slow file: 70733 of 70733 characters, sha aa59b79a1784f959' (characters, not the 70,737 bytes). 'Follow it': the model now holds the file's TOOLS, RULES LOAD, NOTION DATA, ACTIONS, SENDING, LIMITS, SLOW ORDER, SLOW BATCH and steps in context; nothing in B or the file is lost by being in a tool result. The file's RULES LOAD then says 'right after LOCK and before anything else', already past; harmless but stale (D8). RULES LOAD: 5 pages plus 8 routine pages, each with a '<page>: <read> of <total>' line. SLOW BATCH: 40 eligible across STEP 0, 1b, team work, snoozes, STEP 2. Selection: class 1 'recording logistics (prep note, recording link, day-before note)' names mails the SLOW file has no step for (they are FAST's STEP 0r and STEP 0e2; the SLOW SENDING link list has no zencastr link), so Sonnet either finds class 1 empty or selects an item it has no rules to send (D1). Class 2 payments (STEP 1b), class 3 dated promises, class 4 sponsored follow-ups (routine 1), class 5 oldest due. STEP 0 items (feedback, bounces, vendor forms, owner mail, scorecard, edit notes) have no defined action key (only snoozes do), so the model invents keys that won't match next run's carryover (D6), and today's owner mail and the Monday scorecard sort last in class 5 behind a backlog (D6). Carryover: the newest run:zoya-slow: record other than this one; at first run none. 'selected:' written before working, but where is not said: only the final record write is defined, so a crash or compaction loses it (D2). Outcome lines per item, minute check with date -u before each item, stop at minute 22 (11:30). First lines written at the end, then RELEASE. Release around 11:30 to 11:35 if the last item takes under 5 minutes: before 11:38. STEP 2's 'Every due row ends the run sent, held or blocked' and LIMITS' 'works its due list ... until it is empty' still read as 'do all 40', in tension with the fixed 15 (D5).
2b_normal_run_1108.verdict: pass with defects D1, D2, D5, D6, D7, D8

2c_fixture_minute4.trace: Selected 15, 4 settled, the model ends at minute 4 (date -u), no tool error, no cap. SLOW BATCH 4/: the 11 have no sent, completed, held or blocked line, so they go under 'carryover:' and keep Next date. 'A run that ends with selected items lacking an outcome, before minute 22 and with no tool error or cap, is Failed, "early exit at minute 4, 11 of 15 without outcome"'. RUN RECORD agrees: 'Failed: stopped early, ... SLOW BATCH's early exit'. First line: 'eligible 40, oldest due <date> (<row>), selected 15, outcomes sent a, completed b, held c, blocked d, deferred 0, remaining 36'. Summary 'Run zoya-slow <start> JST: Failed'. RELEASE. 17:08 run: carryover = keys under 'carryover:' in the newest run:zoya-slow: record other than its own = the 11:08 record, 11 keys; each still eligible (Next date unchanged) and goes first within its class; the 4 free slots fill by class. The text produces exactly the CTO's result on this path. Two gaps: (1) if the 17:08 slot is Skipped (lock held by the 16:38 FAST run) the next day's 11:08 reads the Skipped record as newest and finds no carryover; the same happens after a 'slow work file unavailable' Failed or a record left at Started (D2). The items stay due and still sort by class and age, so nothing is lost, only the priority. (2) An early-quitting model can avoid Failed by writing the 11 as 'held <why>' or 'blocked <why>' with a free-text why ('not enough of the run'): the outcome grammar has no closed list, so the run would read Completed (D4).
2c_fixture_minute4.verdict: pass on the literal fixture; must fix D2 and D4 for it to hold under the realistic variants

2d_1638_excuse.trace: B's SLOW FILE: 'Its size, the number of rows due and a guess at the time are never a reason not to load it or not to work: only SLOW BATCH's measured minute 22, a cap or a tool error stops the work.' SLOW ORDER repeats it ('the number due' added). RUN RECORD: 'size or context never ends a run early'. A short read fails closed (Failed 'slow file not loaded'). Declining to load is no longer an option the text leaves. Residual routes: free-text 'held'/'blocked'/'deferred (tool error)' lines (D4); and a model that loads only part of the output when all slices go in one Bash call (D7). Context pressure is real: about 70k characters of file plus Rules for Zoya (previously measured at 62k), Wording, Cadences, Client show mails, the follow-ups page and 8 routine pages, then thread reads; on Sonnet this may trigger compaction mid-batch, which is another reason to write 'selected:' to the record early (D2).
2d_1638_excuse.verdict: mostly closed; D4 and D7 close the remaining routes

2e_lock_overlap.trace: 11:08 with the lock held by a 10:38 FAST run: B's LOCK step 3 writes one Activity, Summary 'Run zoya-slow 2026-11-03 11:08 JST: Skipped: lock held by <run id and time>', Source ID run:zoya-slow:<id> (RUN RECORD's Source ID), fetching only Activities, whose id B carries; no SLOW FILE, no reads, no sends, no release (it doesn't hold the lock). The slot does no SLOW work until 17:08. FAST at 11:38 while B holds: A's LOCK writes 'Run zoya ... Skipped: lock held by <B id>'. Neither reconciles. Sent reconcile: A and the file both read 'the earliest run of either Zoya task (run:zoya: or run:zoya-slow: records) that took the lock since the last Completed one (Skipped records don't count)' with a 24-hour floor, so a SLOW Failed or Partial run's unlogged sends are found by the next FAST run and vice versa. 'The last Completed one' is either task's; the 24-hour floor covers the gap. Double send: each action's Sent check plus idempotency key, the action types split FAST (reply, decision, hold) from SLOW (followup, nurture, team), and SLOW's 7-day rule counts FAST's substantive mail from Activities. Daily cap: both count today's JST 'Zoya sent'/'Agent sent' Activities; the lock serialises the tasks so no race. A crashed run that never releases blocks both tasks until the runbook; r13 adds two lock-takers a day, so watch for it in the good-morning check (decision 419).

2f_caps_and_tool_errors.trace: Daily cap reached after item 9: items 10 to 15 'deferred (cap)', no row change ('a cap moves nothing'), under carryover; status Partial. Per-run cap: same path. MCP Emails failing after one retry: mail items 'deferred (tool error)', Notion-only items (snoozes, vendor form rows, Task rows) carry on. Notion failing: every item needs Notion, so all deferred, and the run record's final write may itself fail ('retry once, then report it'): the carryover is lost but items stay due. End status for a tool-error deferral is not named in 4/ ('A cap or minute 22 with items deferred is Partial'); RUN RECORD's 'Partial: a step failed' covers it, but say so in 4/ (D9).
